products.quality: Color-palette layers carry full cut settings; picking a palette color assigns objects; image-on-vector layers auto-split. The reference model for this sector.
Color layers exist but are organizational by default ('don't have any effect on the output'); operations attach to shapes; optional 'Auto Use Layer' binds an operation to every shape on a layer.
No layer concept: docs describe loading a single file/program with global settings; no per-layer or per-color model anywhere in official usage docs.

xTool Studio defines layers by vector stroke color (8 preset colors) but 'layers do not directly establish parameters' — they only speed multi-select; new same-color objects need manual re-assignment.
No settings-layer model; 'creating layers' in docs means z-order stacking via Edit > Send backward/Send to back; cut settings live on individual shapes.

Per layer: Speed, Max/Min Power, passes, interval, air assist, frequency/Q-Pulse (galvo), name, output — plus Common/Advanced tabs per mode in the Cut Settings Editor. Broadest documented set in roster.
CNC analog: per-operation Start/Final Depth, feed rate, plunge rate, spindle speed, auto chip-load, climb/conventional direction. No laser params — CNC-only app.
No per-layer parameters (no layers); only whole-job settings — import-dialog speed/power and a numeric multi-pass repeat counter at send time.

Per-object power, speed, passes plus processing type; Studio adds material thickness measurement. Community guides confirm power/speed/passes as the core triad — narrower than LightBurn's per-layer set.
CNC analog: material/bit-level feed rate, plunge rate, depth per pass; per-shape overall depth. Deliberately small beginner set; no spindle-RPM-per-op breadth in core UI.
Up to 11 Sub-Layers per layer, each with its own mode/power/speed and output toggle; drag tabs to reorder execution; auto-converts legacy Fill+Line projects.
Multiple operations can reference identical shapes — duplicating an operation 'is assigned to the exact same shapes as the original' — giving stacked ops per geometry.
No layers or per-shape operations; a loaded program is one job (repeatable via multi-pass counter only).
Layers hold no parameters and each object carries a single processing type; no sub-layer or stacked-ops feature found in Studio docs. Inferred from absence — flagged.
One cut type per shape; Two-Stage Carves split a job by bit (roughing/detail), not stacked operations on one shape. Inferred from docs — flagged.
Shape Properties window gives per-shape Power Scale — rescales power between Min and Max Power per shape; multi-selection edits all at once. Narrow (power only), widely used for test grids.
Native by construction: operations are assigned to selected shapes directly, so any shape subset gets its own full parameter set.
No object model; settings apply to the whole loaded job.
Native by construction: parameters attach to objects, not layers — per-object settings are the default (and only) model in xTool Studio.
Native: per-shape depth slider and cut type (fill; outline on/inside/outside path) in the Cut menu; tabs auto-added on through-cuts.

.clb libraries: create-from-layer, Assign vs Link (synced/locked), merge, shared network libraries, device-linked. Ships empty — no built-in presets; new users repeatedly surprised, community shares .clb files.

Operations Library saves device-specific operation presets in nestable folders, Apply-to-selection; no material feeds/speeds database documented (a 'Hidden' MaterialLibrary docs page appears to be shared LightBurn doc infrastructure, not a confirmed feature).
No material or preset library appears anywhere in the official usage docs or FAQ. Inferred from absence — flagged.

Strongest bundled offering: official EasySet Library of per-machine, per-material recommended presets ('continuously expanding'), one-click apply; users can define, save, and share custom materials/parameter presets. xTool-hardware-only scope.
Built-in recommended cut settings per machine+material+bit combination; Easel Pro adds Stored Cut Settings that auto-apply to new projects using the same combo.
Drag or up/down layer reorder; 'Sort Cuts Last' auto-orders layers least-likely-to-cut-through first (engrave before cut); per-layer Output toggles.
Operations run top-to-bottom; drag or up/down buttons reorder; per-operation Output toggle controls inclusion in Preview/Start/G-code save.
Executes loaded G-code in file order; no reordering or priority controls documented. Inferred from absence — flagged.

Two modes: Auto Planning (engrave-first algorithm with shortest-path optimization) or 'By layer' manual top-to-bottom ordering via layer-panel drag; Arrange z-order deliberately does not affect processing order.
No native cut-order control; community consensus workaround is splitting designs across workpieces; ordering bugs (outlines before centers) and efficiency feature requests recur on the forum.

Cuts/Layers table with inline editing of pass/speed/power/interval, drag reorder, Output/Show/Air toggles, settings Copy/Paste, right-click context menus on layers and headers — the daily-driver panel this sector is benchmarked against.

Operations Window table (name, mode, tool, output, vacuum/coolant columns) with drag reorder — LightBurn-style ergonomics ported to CNC ops. Product too new (~4 months GA) for community quality consensus.
No cut-settings panel exists; the UI is a command queue, log, and jogging controls around a loaded file.

Right-hand settings panel to 'view or adjust processing parameters such as power and speed' plus framing; parameter depth per panel not documented in detail. Quality signal unknown — no community consensus found.

Settings split between a per-shape Cut menu and a project-level material/bit picker; no consolidated settings table. Deliberately minimal, beginner-oriented. Ergonomics-vs-power judgment inferred — flagged.
